name: Topical Bible Study
description: Answer a focused biblical question by interpreting relevant passages in context before drawing conclusions.

sections.title: Topic and questions
sections.guidance: State the topic, its boundaries and the questions the study should answer. Avoid starting with a conclusion.

sections.title: Relevant Scripture
sections.guidance: Gather representative passages, including those that qualify or appear to challenge an initial view. Note why each is relevant.

sections.title: Examine the passages
sections.guidance: Read each text in its literary, historical and covenantal context. Distinguish direct teaching, narrative description, inference and application.

sections.title: Compare and group findings
sections.guidance: Group the passages by their actual teaching, noting agreements, differences, development and remaining questions.

sections.title: Biblical conclusions
sections.guidance: Answer the opening questions with references. Distinguish what Scripture clearly teaches from reasonable inference and unresolved issues.

sections.title: Application
sections.guidance: Identify concrete implications for belief, worship, relationships and action, grounded in the conclusions.

sections.title: Difficult or balancing texts
sections.guidance: Examine apparently conflicting passages without ignoring their context or forcing a superficial harmonisation.

sections.title: Place in the whole Bible
sections.guidance: Where relevant, consider how the teaching unfolds through the covenants and relates to Christ and the gospel without imposing a connection.
